title: Reuse canonical TypedAxis ordering instead of per-operation label-index maps
finding: TypedAxis already canonicalizes and retains labels as a sorted tuple, but TypedRelationBlock.from_coordinates() and get() rebuilt complete label-to-index dictionaries for both axes before resolving one coordinate or lookup. At the declared 100,000-label axis ceiling this duplicated the full axis label surface during ordinary sparse construction and point lookup even though the retained canonical ordering already supports exact logarithmic membership and index resolution.
primary_claim: Relation-block construction and point lookup now resolve labels directly against the existing sorted TypedAxis labels with bisect_left and retain the public label_index compatibility property without using it internally. Fourfold subject identity, typed plane signatures, CSR canonicalization, semiring behavior, operation bounds and wire contracts remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the canonical sorted axis labels already retained by TypedAxis instead of materializing complete transient dictionaries inside sparse construction and point lookup. Keep label_index only as the existing compatibility surface; do not add a cache, lookup service, alternate axis type, planner, store, registry, scheduler or sparse backend.
acceptance: TypedRelationBlock.from_coordinates does not materialize complete row and column label-index mappings
TypedRelationBlock.get does not materialize complete row and column label-index mappings
